title: Higher Renal Mineralocorticoid Receptor and 11β-hydroxysteroid Dehydrogenase Type 2 Levels Promote Potassium Retention in Female Spontaneously Hypertensive Rats Under MR Blockade
content: Mineralocorticoid receptor (MR) blockade exerts sex-specific effects in hypertension and cardiovascular disease; however, its role in blood pressure regulation in spontaneously hypertensive rats (SHR) remains unclear. We assessed the effects of MR antagonism on blood pressure and electrolyte balance in male and female SHR aged 10-15 weeks. In females, spironolactone increased serum potassium by ~0.4 mmol/L and induced a fourfold rise in serum aldosterone, whereas no changes were observed in males. Plasma renin activity and circulating corticosterone were 19% and 41% lower in females than in males but were unaffected by spironolactone in either sex. Plasma renin activity in SHR was comparable to normotensive Wistar-Kyoto rats. Females exhibited approximately twofold higher renal MR and 1.7-fold greater renal 11β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 2 (11βHSD2) protein levels. MR antagonism did not alter ENaC activity, α-ENaC protein abundance, blood pressure, and amiloride-sensitive urinary electrolyte excretion in either sex. Collectively, higher renal MR and 11β-HSD2 abundance in females may enhance the potassium-sparing effect of MR blockade, which is counterbalanced by a compensatory increase in aldosterone. Low renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system activity in SHR may limit the antihypertensive efficacy of MR antagonists.
